Favourite fruits in the book: mango 3, apple 2, banana 5, grapes 4, guava 1. The most favourite is banana (biggest number 5); the least favourite is guava (smallest number 1).

Worked example

In the transport graph, school bus = 9, car = 3, bicycle = 6, motorcycle = 5. Which is used the most?

Step 1: Compare the counts: 9 is the biggest.

Step 2: 9 belongs to the school bus.

Answer: School bus

Key points

  • Count the pictures row by row.
  • Biggest count = most; smallest count = least.

mcqs.q: In the fruit pictograph, how many students like banana?
mcqs.why: Count the pictures in the banana row: there are 5, the biggest row of the fruit graph.

mcqs.q: Which fruit is the most favourite in the book's graph?
mcqs.why: Banana has the most pictures (5), more than mango 3, grapes 4, apple 2 and guava 1.

mcqs.q: Which fruit is the least favourite?
mcqs.why: Guava has only 1 picture, the smallest count, so guava is the least favourite fruit.

mcqs.q: A pictograph shows information with:
mcqs.why: A pictograph uses pictures or faces in rows; we count the pictures to read the information.

mcqs.q: In the transport graph, how many students use a bicycle?
mcqs.why: Count the faces in the bicycle row: 6 students use a bicycle to come to school.

mcqs.q: Which transport is used the least?
mcqs.why: The car row has only 3 pictures, fewer than bus 9, bicycle 6 and motorcycle 5. Car is least.

mcqs.q: In the animal graph, lion = 9 and bear = 3. The most popular animal is:
mcqs.why: The lion has 9 pictures, the biggest count in the animal graph, so the lion is most popular.

mcqs.q: In the fruit graph of Exercise 1, orange = 8 and apricot = 3. Orange is:
mcqs.why: 8 is the biggest number in that graph (peach 7, pomegranate 6, watermelon 4), so orange is most favourite.

mcqs.q: To read a pictograph, we:
options: Count the pictures in each row
mcqs.why: Each row's pictures must be counted one by one; the count is the number for that thing.

mcqs.q: In the animal graph, how many students like the horse?
mcqs.why: Count the pictures in the horse row of the book's animal graph: there are 8.

lessons.title: More Likely and Less Likely
lessons.notes_html:
Chance words

An event with more chance of happening is more likely. An event with less chance is less likely.

  • Rain under dark clouds: more likely. Rain under a clear sunny sky: less likely.
  • Getting late in a heavy traffic jam: more likely.
  • Getting sick for a child wet in the rain eating an ice lolly: more likely.
  • Weak eyesight from using a mobile in dim light: more likely.

Worked example

Is rain more likely under dark clouds or under a clear sky?

Step 1: Dark clouds are a sign that rain is coming.

Step 2: A clear sky gives rain very little chance.

Answer: More likely under dark clouds

Key points

  • More likely = more chance.
  • Less likely = less chance.

mcqs.q: Rain is more likely when the sky has:
mcqs.why: Dark clouds bring rain, so rain has more chance — it is more likely under dark clouds.

mcqs.q: Getting late is more likely:
mcqs.why: A traffic jam slows everyone down, so reaching late has more chance — it is more likely.

mcqs.q: A child wet in the rain eating an ice lolly is more likely to:
mcqs.why: Being wet in rain and eating something cold gives sickness more chance, so it is more likely.

mcqs.q: Using a mobile in dim, dark light makes weak eyesight:
mcqs.why: Straining the eyes in dark light harms them, so weak eyesight becomes more likely.

mcqs.q: 'Less likely' means the event has:
mcqs.why: Less likely describes an event whose chance of happening is small, like rain in a clear sky.

mcqs.q: Reading in good light and sleeping well makes weak eyesight:
mcqs.why: Good habits protect the eyes, so weak eyesight has less chance — it is less likely.

mcqs.q: On an empty clear road, getting late is:
mcqs.why: With no traffic to slow us down, reaching late has little chance — it is less likely.

mcqs.q: A healthy child playing in the park is ___ to get sick.
mcqs.why: A healthy, dry, playing child has little chance of sickness compared with a wet child — less likely.

mcqs.q: Which event is more likely?
mcqs.why: Of these, only rain under dark clouds has a strong chance; the others have little or no chance.

mcqs.q: 'More likely' means the event has:
mcqs.why: More likely is used when an event has a greater chance of happening than not happening.

lessons.title: Hands-On STEAM Games
lessons.notes_html:
Maths by playing (teacher-led)

  • Fruit Shop game: buying fruit is addition in real life.
  • Bowling game: 10 cups stand as pins; remaining pins = 10 − fallen pins.
  • Time Hunt game: find the clock that shows the asked time.

Worked example

In the Fruit Shop game, you buy 2 apples and then 3 apples. How many in all?

Step 1: Join the two buys: 2 + 3.

Step 2: Count 3 forward from 2: 3, 4, 5.

Answer: 5 apples

Key points

  • Games use the same adding, subtracting and time reading.

mcqs.q: In the Fruit Shop game, buying 2 apples and 3 apples makes how many in all?
mcqs.why: Add the two buys: 2 + 3 = 5. Count forward from 2: 3, 4, 5 — five apples in all.

mcqs.q: In Bowling, 10 pins stand and 4 fall down. How many remain?
mcqs.why: Remaining pins = total - fallen = 10 - 4 = 6 pins still standing.

mcqs.q: In the Time Hunt, the 3 o'clock clock has its short hand at:
mcqs.why: At 3 o'clock the short hour hand points at 3 and the long minute hand points at 12.

mcqs.q: In Bowling, if 0 pins fall, the remaining pins are:
mcqs.why: Remaining = 10 - 0 = 10. Subtracting zero leaves all ten pins standing.

mcqs.q: In the Fruit Shop game, buying 4 oranges and 4 oranges makes:
mcqs.why: Join the buys: 4 + 4 = 8. Count forward from 4: 5, 6, 7, 8 — eight oranges.

mcqs.q: In Bowling, 10 pins stand and 7 fall. Remaining = ?
mcqs.why: Remaining = 10 - 7 = 3 pins. Count back from 10 by 7: 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3.

mcqs.q: The Time Hunt asks for 3 o'clock. The long hand of that clock is at:
mcqs.why: For any o'clock time the long minute hand points at 12; only the short hand moves to 3.

mcqs.q: These games are led by:
mcqs.why: The book marks the STEAM activities as teacher-led: the teacher runs the games for the class.

mcqs.q: In the Fruit Shop game, buying 1 mango and 5 mangoes makes:
mcqs.why: Add the buys: 1 + 5 = 6. Count forward from 5 by 1: 6 — six mangoes in all.

mcqs.q: In Bowling, remaining pins are found by:
mcqs.why: Some pins fall from the 10 standing pins, so what remains is 10 minus the fallen pins.

lessons.title: AI Puzzle Games
lessons.notes_html:
Playing with the computer (teacher-led)

  • AI riddle: 'You have 3 apples and AI gives you 2 more — how many now?' It is an addition story.
  • Digital Domino: add the dots on both sides.
  • AI Balance: think — is an apple heavier than a pencil? Yes.
  • Cash Register game: make amounts with coins and notes: Rs. 20 = Rs. 10 + Rs. 10; Rs. 50 = one Rs. 50 note.

Worked example

A domino has 4 dots on one side and 2 dots on the other. Total dots?

Step 1: Add both sides: 4 + 2.

Step 2: Count 2 forward from 4: 5, 6.

Answer: 6 dots

Key points

  • The games practise adding, comparing weight and making money amounts.

mcqs.q: AI riddle: You have 3 apples and AI gives you 2 more. How many now?
mcqs.why: Join the two groups: 3 + 2 = 5. Count forward from 3: 4, 5 — five apples now.

mcqs.q: A domino has 4 dots and 2 dots. Total dots = ?
mcqs.why: Add the dots of both sides: 4 + 2 = 6 dots in total on the domino.

mcqs.q: AI Balance asks: Is an apple heavier than a pencil?
mcqs.why: An apple is a fruit with much more weight than a thin pencil, so yes, the apple is heavier.

mcqs.q: How can you make Rs. 20 in the Cash Register game?
mcqs.why: Two ten-rupee pieces join to make twenty: 10 + 10 = 20 rupees.

mcqs.q: How can you make Rs. 50 in the Cash Register game?
mcqs.why: The simplest way is a single note of fifty: one Rs. 50 note makes Rs. 50.

mcqs.q: A domino has 3 dots and 3 dots. Total dots = ?
mcqs.why: Add both sides: 3 + 3 = 6. Count forward from 3: 4, 5, 6 — six dots.

mcqs.q: AI riddle: You have 5 toffees and AI gives you 4 more. How many now?
mcqs.why: Join the groups: 5 + 4 = 9. Count forward from 5: 6, 7, 8, 9 — nine toffees.

mcqs.q: In the Cash Register game, Rs. 10 + Rs. 10 makes:
mcqs.why: Adding the two amounts: 10 + 10 = 20, so the register shows Rs. 20.

mcqs.q: A domino has 5 dots and 1 dot. Total dots = ?
mcqs.why: Add the two sides: 5 + 1 = 6 dots in total on this domino.

mcqs.q: The AI activities in the book are:
mcqs.why: Like the STEAM games, the AI puzzle activities are marked teacher-led in the book.

lessons.title: Maths Websites for Practice
lessons.notes_html:

How to use them

mcqs.q: Which of these websites is given in the book for maths practice?

mcqs.q: How many websites are listed at the end of the book?

mcqs.q: The book says to practise on these sites with:

mcqs.q: Which of these is in the book's website list?
mcqs.why: IXL is the second name in the book's list of maths practice websites for grade 1.

mcqs.why: The book is for grade 1, so we open the grade 1 maths pages that match our class.

mcqs.q: Which pair is fully from the book's list?
mcqs.why: Math Games and ABCya are both in the book's list of eight practice websites.

lessons.title: Counting and Writing Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Workbook counting practice

The workbook practises counting fingers, things and shapes, writing missing numbers and number lines.

  • Fingers on the hands: write 1 to 5, then 6 to 10.
  • Descending stairs: 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.
  • An empty bowl shows the number 0.
  • Missing numbers: 1, 2, 3, ___, 5 → 4; in descending ___, 8, ___, 6 → 9, 7.

Worked example

Count the things: ants, chilies, pigeons, coconuts in the workbook picture.

Step 1: Count each group one by one.

Step 2: Ants 3, chilies 5, pigeons 6, coconuts 4.

Answer: 3, 5, 6, 4

Key points

  • Tick the bigger number: of 2 and 7, tick 7; of 9 and 6, tick 9.

mcqs.q: What number does an empty bowl show?
mcqs.why: An empty bowl has nothing in it, and the number for nothing is 0, read as zero.

mcqs.q: Fill the missing number: 1, 2, 3, ___, 5
mcqs.why: Forward counting: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The missing number between 3 and 5 is 4.

mcqs.q: Descending stairs: 9, 8, ___, 6, ___, 4, 3, ___, ___. First missing number?
mcqs.why: Backward counting from 9: 9, 8, 7, 6... The first missing number after 8 is 7.

mcqs.q: Of the numbers 2 and 7, the bigger number is:
mcqs.why: Compare: 7 is more than 2, so we tick 7 as the bigger number, as in Assessment 3.

mcqs.q: Count the fingers: a hand showing six fingers in the workbook is written:
mcqs.why: Count the raised fingers one by one up to the last: the sixth finger gives the number 6.

mcqs.q: In the workbook box, chairs = 3 and shirts = 8 (book's key). How many shirts?
mcqs.why: As per the book's answer key, the shirts in the box are counted as 8 (and the chairs as 3).

mcqs.q: Fill the missing numbers in descending order: ___, 8, ___, 6
mcqs.why: Going down: 9, 8, 7, 6. The number before 8 is 9 and between 8 and 6 is 7.

mcqs.q: How many shapes are traced in workbook Exercise 2?
mcqs.why: The traced shapes are square, square, circle, oval, triangle, triangle — 6 shapes in all.

mcqs.q: How many dotted lines are traced in workbook Exercise 1?
mcqs.why: Counting all the dotted lines in the exercise gives 18 lines to trace with the pencil.

mcqs.q: Of the numbers 9 and 6, tick the bigger:
mcqs.why: 9 is greater than 6, so the tick goes on 9, as in the workbook's Assessment 3.

lessons.title: Number Bonds of 5 and 10
lessons.notes_html:
Number bonds

A number bond shows two parts that join to make a whole number.

Bonds of 5: 5 = 3 + 2, 5 = 1 + 4, 5 = 2 + 3, 5 = 0 + 5.

Bonds of 10: 10 = 6 + 4, 10 = 8 + 2, 10 = 1 + 9, 10 = 9 + 1, 10 = 7 + 3.

Worked example

Complete the bond: 10 = 8 + ___.

Step 1: The missing part = 10 − 8.

Step 2: 10 − 8 = 2. Check: 8 + 2 = 10. ✓

Answer: 2

Key points

  • Missing part = whole − known part.
  • Learn the bonds of 10 by heart.

mcqs.q: Complete the bond: 5 = 3 + ___
mcqs.why: Missing part = 5 - 3 = 2. Check: 3 + 2 = 5, so the bond is completed by 2.

mcqs.q: Complete the bond: 10 = 6 + ___
mcqs.why: Missing part = 10 - 6 = 4. Check: 6 + 4 = 10, so the missing partner is 4.

mcqs.q: Complete the bond: 10 = 9 + ___
mcqs.why: Missing part = 10 - 9 = 1. Check: 9 + 1 = 10, so the bond needs 1.

mcqs.q: Complete the bond: 5 = 1 + ___
mcqs.why: Missing part = 5 - 1 = 4. Check: 1 + 4 = 5, one of the book's bonds of 5.

mcqs.q: Complete the bond: 10 = 2 + ___
mcqs.why: Missing part = 10 - 2 = 8. Check: 2 + 8 = 10, as in workbook Assessment 1.

mcqs.q: Complete the bond: 10 = 7 + ___
mcqs.why: Missing part = 10 - 7 = 3. Check: 7 + 3 = 10, as in workbook Assessment 1.

mcqs.q: Which is a correct bond of 5?
mcqs.why: Check the sums: 2 + 3 = 5 is correct. The others make 8, 10 and 2, not 5.

mcqs.q: Complete the bond: 10 = 4 + ___
mcqs.why: Missing part = 10 - 4 = 6. Check: 4 + 6 = 10, one of the workbook's bonds of 10.

mcqs.q: Complete the bond: 5 = 0 + ___
mcqs.why: Missing part = 5 - 0 = 5. Check: 0 + 5 = 5, as shown in Assessment 3 of the workbook.

mcqs.q: A number bond shows:
options: Two parts that make a whole
mcqs.why: A bond splits a whole number into two parts; adding the parts gives the whole again.

lessons.title: Numbers in Blocks: Tens and Ones
lessons.notes_html:
Reading block pictures

In the workbook, numbers are shown with blocks: a long block of ten and single one-blocks. Count the tens first (each = 10), then the ones.

Worked example

A picture shows 2 ten-blocks and 3 one-blocks (the book's example style: example 21 has 2 tens and 1 one). What is the number for 2 tens and 3 ones?

Step 1: Tens: 2 blocks = 20.

Step 2: Add the ones: 20 + 3 = 23.

Answer: 23

Splitting numbers

13 = 10 + 3, 12 = 10 + 2, 14 = 10 + 4, 10 = 10 + 0. And 10 + 9 = 19.

Key points

  • Count tens by 10, then count the ones.
  • Example blocks in the book: 14, 21, 31, 41 ... up to 100.

mcqs.q: A block picture shows 3 tens and 3 ones (workbook style). The number is:
mcqs.why: Count the tens: 3 blocks = 30; add 3 ones: 30 + 3 = 33, one of the workbook's answers.

mcqs.q: Split 13 into 10 + ___
mcqs.why: 13 is one ten and 3 ones: 13 = 10 + 3. The ones part left after the ten is 3.
One ten plus nine ones makes the number 19, from the workbook's Exercise 17.

mcqs.q: A block picture shows 9 tens and 0 ones (workbook Ex28 style). The number is:
mcqs.why: Nine ten-blocks are 9 × 10 = 90 with no loose ones, giving the number 90.

mcqs.q: A block picture shows 10 tens. The number is:
mcqs.why: Ten blocks of ten make one hundred: 10 tens = 100, the last workbook block number.

mcqs.q: Split 14 into 10 + ___
mcqs.why: 14 = one ten + 4 ones, so 14 = 10 + 4, from the workbook's splitting exercise.

mcqs.q: 6 + 10 = ? (workbook Assessment 5)
mcqs.why: Adding ten to 6 moves it one ten up: 6 + 10 = 16, as in the workbook assessment.

mcqs.q: A block picture shows 4 tens and 7 ones. The number is:
mcqs.why: Tens first: 4 blocks = 40; ones: 7. Joined: 40 + 7 = 47, a workbook Assessment 2 number.

mcqs.q: 10 + 10 = ? (workbook Assessment 5)
mcqs.why: Two tens joined make 20: 10 + 10 = 20, as in the workbook's Assessment 5.

mcqs.q: A block picture shows 8 tens and 6 ones (Assessment 2 style). The number is:
mcqs.why: 8 tens = 80 and 6 ones = 6; together 80 + 6 = 86, one of the Assessment 2 block numbers.

lessons.title: Workbook Addition Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Adding in the workbook

The workbook adds step by step: first +1 and +4, then adding zero, then vertical sums.

  • 2 + 1 = 3, 3 + 1 = 4, 4 + 1 = 5, 1 + 2 = 3.
  • 2 + 4 = 6, 3 + 4 = 7, 4 + 4 = 8, 1 + 5 = 6.
  • Adding zero: 7 + 0 = 7, 5 + 0 = 5, 8 + 0 = 8.
  • Vertical: 3 + 5 = 8, 1 + 8 = 9, 2 + 6 = 8, 4 + 0 = 4.

Worked example

Add (workbook sample style): 1 + 4.

Step 1: Start at 1... or count 4 forward from the bigger number 4: 5.

Answer: 5 (the book's given sample)

Key points

  • Count forward from the bigger number.
  • + 0 never changes the number.

mcqs.q: 2 + 4 = ? (workbook Exercise 30)
mcqs.why: Count 4 forward from 2: 3, 4, 5, 6. So 2 + 4 = 6, as in the workbook exercise.

mcqs.q: 7 + 0 = ? (workbook Exercise 31)
mcqs.why: Adding zero joins nothing, so the number stays 7: 7 + 0 = 7.

mcqs.q: 3 + 5 = ? (workbook vertical Exercise 32)
mcqs.why: Count forward from 5 by 3: 6, 7, 8. So 3 + 5 = 8.

mcqs.q: 1 + 2 = ? (workbook Assessment 8)
mcqs.why: Count 2 forward from 1: 2, 3. So 1 + 2 = 3, from workbook Assessment 8.

mcqs.q: 4 + 4 = ? (workbook Exercise 30)
mcqs.why: Count 4 forward from 4: 5, 6, 7, 8. So 4 + 4 = 8.

mcqs.q: 3 + 3 = ? (workbook Assessment 8)
mcqs.why: Count forward from 3 by 3: 4, 5, 6. So 3 + 3 = 6, from workbook Assessment 8.

mcqs.q: 6 + 2 = ? (workbook Assessment 8)
mcqs.why: Count 2 forward from 6: 7, 8. So 6 + 2 = 8, from workbook Assessment 8.

mcqs.q: 2 + 7 = ? (workbook Assessment 8)
mcqs.why: Count 7 forward from 2 (or 2 forward from 7): 8, 9. So 2 + 7 = 9.

mcqs.q: 5 + 3 = ? (workbook G1 Assessment 3)

mcqs.q: 8 + 1 = ? (workbook G1 Assessment 3)

lessons.title: Workbook Subtraction Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Subtracting in the workbook

The workbook subtracts step by step, including subtracting zero and vertical sums.

  • 3 − 2 = 1, 6 − 3 = 3, 5 − 2 = 3, 6 − 4 = 2.
  • 7 − 4 = 3, 8 − 6 = 2, 9 − 8 = 1, 7 − 5 = 2.
  • Subtracting zero: 1 − 0 = 1, 3 − 0 = 3, 7 − 0 = 7, 0 − 0 = 0.
  • Vertical: 5 − 3 = 2, 8 − 1 = 7, 6 − 2 = 4, 4 − 4 = 0.

Worked example

Subtract (workbook sample style): 5 − 1.

Step 1: Count 1 back from 5.

Answer: 4 (the book's given sample)

Key points

  • Count backward for subtraction.
  • − 0 never changes the number; a number minus itself is 0.
